Series::isneginf¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series Series::isneginf() const

Identify Only Negative Infinity¶

isneginf() performs an elementwise directional infinity test. An output lane is true exactly when the corresponding receiver value is negative infinity. Finite negative numbers, signed zero, positive infinity, and NaN are all false.

Use this method when the sign of an infinite result carries meaning, such as distinguishing negative overflow from positive overflow. Use isinf() when both directions should be selected, or isfinite() when the desired mask is the complement of all infinities and NaN values.

The output is a newly allocated Boolean Series with the same rank, shape, element order, and platform as the receiver. Floating dtypes can contain the matching value. Integral and Boolean receivers are accepted and produce an all-false result. Complex receivers are rejected because a complex number has no single ordered sign; test a deliberate component with real() or imag() when component-wise classification is intended.

The predicate is non-differentiable. A Boolean result does not carry a reverse node, even when the receiver tracks sensitivity. Use the mask to select or replace values in a subsequent expression, not as a numeric surrogate for a derivative.

Examples¶

Example 1. Only the first lane is negative infinity. Neither negative zero nor NaN matches.

const double inf = std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
const double nan = std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN();
auto x = pluss::make_series({-inf, -1.0, -0.0, 0.0, 1.0, inf, nan});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x.isneginf());

Output¶

Series(shape=[7], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=7, contiguous=true)
data=[true, false, false, false, false, false, false]

Example 2. Higher-rank shape is preserved lane for lane.

const double inf = std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
const double nan = std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN();
auto x = pluss::make_series({{-inf, 2.0}, {inf, nan}});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x.isneginf());

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡  true false ⎤
⎣ false false ⎦

Example 3. Integers cannot encode infinity, so every lane is false.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({-2, 0, 2}).isneginf());

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[false, false, false]

Example 4. Combine the two directional predicates when later logic needs an all-infinity mask while retaining the option to inspect direction separately.

const double inf = std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
const double nan = std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN();
auto x = pluss::make_series({-inf, -1.0, -0.0, 0.0, 1.0, inf, nan});
pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    x.isneginf().logical_or(x.isposinf()));

Output¶

Series(shape=[7], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=7, contiguous=true)
data=[true, false, false, false, false, true, false]

Example 5. Complex input requires an explicit component choice.

try {
  using Complex = std::complex<double>;
  const double inf = std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
  (void)pluss::make_series(std::vector<Complex>{{inf, 0.0}}, {1})
      .isneginf();
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  const std::string message = e.what();
  std::cout << message.substr(0, message.find('\n'));
}

Output¶

isneginf: complex input is not supported

See Also¶

  • isposinf() selects positive infinity only.

  • isinf() selects infinity in either direction.

  • isfinite() selects finite values.

  • isnan() selects not-a-number values.
